chapter: Family, marching bands and the tavern
title: Profit, the Altadena neighborhood and selling out
summary: The tavern made good profit early, he bought the property, ran it to 1971, leased it a year and then sold everything.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Anyway, we went throught it and a profit was made.
How was the business? Did you do good?
It was good, we made a good profit the first three or four
years. My wife and I would just take off and take a trip, because we didn't need the money.
A lot of people in business, they go to the cash register and give the wife to go to the grocery store; well, I didn't have to do that.
You were in a very fortunate position that you had worked with the L.A. Unified School District and you had a retirement and other additional income.
That's right, which I could live on.
I was the only one up there where the delivery man didn't wait for his pay, all he had to do was sign. I was the only one, because all the rest of the places had to pay cash before he would leave.
The black population was very small at this time, wasn't it? There weren't very many blacks in Altadena at that time, in the early sixties?

Well, not too many, because we bought the place from a white guy and the reason he sold it was because the neighborhood was changing. That's why I didn't have to advertise because the negroes still living there didn't go in there as long as a white man owned it.
When I opened it here they come.
Yes, they were very glad to have some place to go and socialize.
I let my help off on Sundays, on Sunday my wife and I would run it ourselves, just the two of us on a Sunday.
You'd run it on Sunday?
Yes.
A lot different from running a club nowadays, isn't it? This was what, twenty years ago. Things have changed so much.
This was '65,
Are there any taverns now in the area?
There was another one on the same block I was, which was still owned by white.
Is it still there now?
It's still there now, but a colored boy is operating it now. My old place is still there too, but somebody else has it. We did so well that after two years we bought the property.
Did you lease it out or did you sell it subsequently?

I ran it for six years; I ran it from '65 to '71, then I leased it out for another year and then the second year that was renting it from me got slow in his pay and somebody suggested why don't you go back and open it and I said no, I had enough and so I just locked the
And you sold it?
I sold everything, the land and everything.
